success_patterns: Rewrite nested quantifiers in order and track what each witness may depend on; this distinguishes one fixed choice that must work for every target from a fresh choice for each target.
Treat stated dependencies of constants as part of the claim: an absolute constant uniform across parameters is stronger than one allowed to depend on them.
Compare the exact scope and strength of viable options, including equality versus a one-sided bound and an almost-everywhere claim versus an everywhere claim.

patch.reasoning: The clearest reusable success was catching the witness-dependence and constant-dependence differences between near-identical options. A narrowly actionable rule captures that behavior without repeating the previous broad audit guidance.

edits.content:
## Track Witness and Constant Dependencies
When options differ in quantifier order, rewrite the quantifiers and note what each existential witness may depend on. In particular, distinguish one fixed choice required to work for every target from a choice made separately after each target is specified. Also record exactly which parameters a bound's constant may depend on: “absolute” or uniform in a parameter is a substantive strengthening.
